newsitem.title: USA: Noble Roman's in default on facility.
newsitem.headline: Noble Roman's in default on facility.

text.p: Noble Roman's Inc, a restaurant franchiser, said Friday it was in default of its $14 million senior credit facility.

The company said it is negotiating with Provident Bank to convert a substantial portion of that facility to equity and is negotiating with other financial institutions to have them purchase the credit facility and convert a substantial portion to equity.

"These are complex negotiations and there can be no assurance that they will be successful," the company said in a news release, adding that because of the events, the company's auditors qualified their opinion as to these uncertainties.

The company also reported a loss of $3.9 million, or $0.94 a share for 1996, including $880,862 for costs associated with a withdrawn acquisition of a pizza chain in the Northeast, $673,157 from the charge-off of notes receivable, and $874,768 valuation allowance established against deferred tax credits. Comparable figures form the previous year were not immediately available.
In May, the company closed 18 of its restaurants as part of a plan to restructure the company.

The company also said Friday it began a new franchising concept in December, with convenience stores selling fresh baked Noble Roman's pizza and breadsticks. So far in 1997, 10 such franchise units have been opened and the company has signed contracts for the opening of about 40 more in 1997, Noble roman's said.
The company said it receives up front fees and commissions for each franchise as well as seven percent of sales each month as a royalty.
Noble roman's shares were down 2/16 at 13/16 Friday.
